items.title: Recognize managed global-thin projects as activity-log writable roots
items.context: The heartbeat child process can run session_brief in a global-thin project, but cli-engine writeLog currently gates activity logging on hasProjectConfigFile(), whose config filename set only includes lattice.config.json. Add an explicit helper for runtime/log root detection that accepts .lattice/lattice.json with assetMode global-thin without teaching loadConfig() to parse that file as canonical project config.

happy.desc: A managed global-thin project with .lattice/lattice.json declaring assetMode=global-thin and no lattice.config.json runs a heartbeat/log-producing read-only command and writes a current row to that project root .lattice/activity.jsonl. WHY: proves runtime activity-root detection accepts the managed global-thin manifest.

edge.desc: The global-thin runtime/log-root helper remains separate from canonical configuration loading: loadConfig/findProjectRoot behavior still requires lattice.config.json for canonical project config fields and does not parse .lattice/lattice.json as a substitute project config. WHY: prevents managed adapter metadata from becoming canonical workflow config.

adversarial.desc: Directories with no lattice.config.json and no valid managed global-thin .lattice/lattice.json, including malformed or wrong-assetMode manifests, are not promoted to writable activity roots and do not gain stray .lattice/activity.jsonl logs. WHY: prevents unrelated directories from becoming Proofbound roots accidentally.

items.userSees: In a global-thin project, `lattice codex verify` reaches `Global fallback heartbeat` and reports a codex/global-fallback heartbeat instead of `no activity heartbeat for session ...`.

verificationEvidence.note: Focused smoke passed and includes a managed global-thin root with only .lattice/lattice.json assetMode=global-thin; session_brief writes .lattice/activity.jsonl with source=codex.
Build passed and smoke asserts loadConfig on a global-thin-only root keeps defaults from canonical lattice.config.json behavior rather than parsing .lattice/lattice.json.
Smoke covers malformed .lattice/lattice.json and wrong assetMode roots and asserts no .lattice/activity.jsonl is created.

items.title: Cover canonical and global-thin activity logging behavior with regression tests
items.context: Add focused regression or smoke coverage proving canonical lattice.config.json projects still log activity, global-thin managed projects log activity, and unrelated directories do not become project roots accidentally.

happy.desc: A focused regression test proves a normal canonical project containing lattice.config.json still writes successful command activity to <root>/.lattice/activity.jsonl. WHY: preserves the existing canonical activity logging behavior while changing runtime root detection.

edge.desc: A focused regression test proves a managed global-thin project containing .lattice/lattice.json with assetMode=global-thin, and no lattice.config.json or local bin wrappers, writes successful command activity to <root>/.lattice/activity.jsonl. WHY: covers the new global-thin heartbeat path directly.

adversarial.desc: A focused regression test proves an unrelated directory without canonical config and without a valid managed global-thin manifest does not create or append .lattice/activity.jsonl and is not treated as a project root. WHY: guards against over-broad root detection and accidental writes outside managed projects.

items.userSees: The focused smoke output completes without assertion failures after proving canonical projects log activity, managed global-thin projects log activity, and malformed/unmanaged roots do not create `.lattice/activity.jsonl`.

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke creates a canonical lattice.config.json root and verifies session_brief activity is written to .lattice/activity.jsonl.
Smoke creates a global-thin-only root with .lattice/lattice.json assetMode=global-thin and no lattice.config.json, then verifies session_brief activity is written.
Smoke creates malformed and wrong-assetMode .lattice/lattice.json roots and verifies no .lattice/activity.jsonl is created.

items.title: Verify the solver-visible global-thin Codex adapter smoke passes
items.context: After building the CLI and running relevant tests, rerun lattice codex verify in /Users/jek/Documents/Work/deepswe-pos-codex-gpt55-run/solver-visible to confirm the Global fallback heartbeat no longer fails for missing activity heartbeat.

happy.desc: After rebuilding the Proofbound CLI and running the relevant local regression tests, lattice codex verify passes when executed in /Users/jek/Documents/Work/deepswe-pos-codex-gpt55-run/solver-visible. WHY: proves the user-visible global-thin Codex adapter smoke succeeds in the originally failing project.

edge.desc: The solver-visible smoke confirms the command path is appropriate for global-thin projects: local bin wrappers and .lattice-codex assets are not required, and the verified CLI version/build corresponds to the fixed worktree rather than a stale global install. WHY: avoids a false pass from the wrong adapter mode or stale binary.

adversarial.desc: The solver-visible smoke explicitly rules out the prior failure signature: Global fallback heartbeat must not report a missing activity heartbeat for the codex-check-global session, and the resulting activity evidence must show codex/global-fallback attribution in .lattice/activity.jsonl. WHY: prevents accepting a generic verify pass that skipped the broken heartbeat path.

items.userSees: From `/Users/jek/Documents/Work/deepswe-pos-codex-gpt55-run/solver-visible`, `lattice codex verify` exits successfully and the output does not contain `Global fallback heartbeat: no activity heartbeat for session`.

verificationEvidence.note: Using a temporary executable lattice wrapper pointed at the rebuilt B-783c worktree dist, solver-visible `lattice codex verify` exited 0 with `✓ Codex adapter checks passed (8/8 pass)`.

Transcript showed `command -v lattice` resolved to `/tmp/lattice-b783c-bin.t9gEsv/lattice`, a wrapper delegating to /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/.worktrees/B-783c/packages/main/dist/cli.js, so the smoke used the fixed worktree build rather than the stale installed global binary.

Verify output did not contain the prior `no activity heartbeat for session` failure. The solver-visible activity log contains session codex-check-global-1783555223544 with source=codex, entrypoint=global-fallback, tool=session_brief, status=ok.
